Irvine Taiwanese Presbyterian Church (IRVINE台灣基督長老教會)
Summary
蒙上帝的恩典和祝福，我們是一群從台灣出生，蒙神帶領來到美國，經歷跨文化的衝擊，認真接受專業教育訓練與努力工作並培育子女，又蒙神眷顧及恩典滿滿的基督徒。我們大都從全美國退休，移居離台灣最近及安全舒適誼居的Irvine及Laguna Woods Village。我們愛台灣、愛美國、我們相愛相扶持，並努力遵行上帝的旨意，繼續尋求上帝的旨意，希望我們還能多為主做工。 邀請您來到我們這愛的大家庭，一起把上帝的愛帶到Irvine我們教會與世界的每個角落。 自從我們得到了這間兄弟教會Geneva Presbyterian Church的愛心和包容，我們於2012年開始搬到Laguna village CA後，就在這個教會的Chapel做禮拜敬拜上帝，宣講主的福音，相愛相扶持過著黃金的歲月。

Albert Chapter 1 Audiobook — Consent & Recording Kit
This page is the execution kit for producing Chapter 1 audiobook narration using Albert’s voice with explicit permission and source traceability.
1) Written Consent Template (send first)
I, [Full Name], give permission to the Echo/Echopedia team to use my voice for narration of:

Work: “Toward A Community of Hope”
Scope: Chapter 1 (Formosan in Formosa Yesterday)
Usage: Echopedia website playback and archival historical education use
Processing: voice recording cleanup and/or AI voice synthesis based on approved samples
Duration: [one-time release / ongoing until revoked]
Revocation: I may request removal or replacement in future releases
Attribution: [How name should appear]

Signature: ____________________
Date: ____________________
Preferred Contact: ____________________
2) Spoken Consent Script (record verbatim)
“My name is [Name]. Today is [Date]. I authorize the Echo/Echopedia team to use my recorded voice for Chapter 1 of Toward A Community of Hope for publication on Echopedia. I understand this may include audio enhancement and AI-assisted synthesis based on my approved recordings.”
3) Recording Requirements (preferred)

Quiet room, no speakerphone, no background music
File format: WAV (preferred), mono, 16kHz or 24kHz+
Total sample target for cloning: 10–30 minutes
Speaking style: natural pace, clear articulation, normal conversational warmth
Include Taiwan/TAHS name pronunciations in sample set

4) Sample Prompt Set (for voice quality)
Please record:

60–90 seconds reading your normal introduction
2–3 paragraphs from Chapter 1
1 paragraph with names/places (Taiwan, Formosa, Los Angeles, Presbyterian, etc.)
1 paragraph with emotional variation (reflective/hopeful tone)

5) Twilio Outreach Message (short version)
Hi Albert — we’re preparing a Chapter 1 audiobook for Echopedia and would love to use your voice with your explicit permission. If you’re open, we’ll send a simple consent note and a short recording guide (10–30 min clean sample). We can also schedule a quick call to walk through it. Thank you!
6) Quality Gate Before Full Chapter
Before full production, produce a 60–90 second pilot and check:

Pronunciation accuracy
Natural pacing
No clipping/noise artifacts
Approval from stakeholders

Status update:

Full Chapter 1 narration has now been published at Albert Chapter 1 Audiobook（第一章有聲版）.

7) Publication Metadata (required on page)

Narrator / voice attribution
Consent status/date
Audio version/date
Source confidence note
Link to this kit page

Dr. Albert S. Lai (賴信雄)

people/chen-meihui.title: Chen Meihui (陳美蕙)
people/chen-meihui.content:
Chen Meihui (陳美蕙)
Chen Meihui (陳美蕙, Rev. Chen / 陳牧師) was identified in Irvine Taiwanese Presbyterian Church (爾灣台灣基督長老教會) official history as the pastor who took up ITPC pastoral leadership after 張宣信牧師 concluded his long tenure in 2020.
ITPC Role
The official ITPC history states that 張宣信牧師 left ITPC in June 2020 after twenty-one years of service and that 陳美蕙牧師 was called immediately afterward to continue pastoral ministry without interruption. The document describes her as having substantial ability and experience, while giving no extended biography in the extracted text.
Wider Source Signals
GSTPC bulletin ingestion also captured 陳美蕙牧師 / Pastor Chen as a sermon speaker in a 2020 Taiwanese Presbyterian bulletin context. This supports her presence in regional Taiwanese Presbyterian church-source material, though it should not be treated as a full biography.
Current-Leadership Note
The ITPC official site’s 2025–2026 pastor page lists 李輔仁牧師 (Rev. Fu-Jen Li) as current pastor. For that reason, this page records 陳美蕙牧師 as a historical ITPC pastoral leader rather than the current pastor.
Source Notes and Confidence

Primary source: official ITPC history document, “Irvine 台灣基督長老教會的歷史,” linked from the church About page and captured from the official website crawl on 2026-06-06.
Supporting wiki source corpus: GSTPC bulletin pages mentioning 陳美蕙牧師 / Pastor Chen as a sermon speaker.
Source confidence: high for the 2020 ITPC succession note; medium for wider ministry context until more independent biographical sources are added.
Romanization note: “Chen Meihui” is a Mandarin pinyin romanization of 陳美蕙; source excerpts also use the English form “Pastor Chen.” Future correction is welcome if a preferred full English romanization is documented.

people/guo-yingyan.content:
Guo Yingyan (郭應言)
Guo Yingyan (郭應言, Rev. Guo / 郭牧師) was a pastor connected with the early development of Irvine Taiwanese Presbyterian Church (爾灣台灣基督長老教會). The church’s official history identifies him as a pastor who served ITPC after the departure of the founding-stage pastor 鄭泉聲牧師.
ITPC Role
The ITPC history document states that after 鄭泉聲牧師 returned to Japan, the congregation invited nearby pastors to help with pastoral care until 郭應言牧師 was called approximately a year later. It describes 郭應言牧師 as previously serving at a “House of Christ” church context and notes that he resigned after about one year because he was not accustomed to the Presbyterian church system.
Historical Significance
郭應言牧師’s brief service reflects the transitional period between ITPC’s founding independence and its later full-time pastoral stability. His tenure sits in the late-1990s period when the congregation was still worshiping at Creekside Fellowship Church and seeking durable pastoral leadership.
Source Notes and Confidence

Primary source: official ITPC history document, “Irvine 台灣基督長老教會的歷史,” linked from the church About page and captured from the official website crawl on 2026-06-06.
Source confidence: high for his appearance in ITPC’s pastoral chronology; limited for wider biography because no independent biographical source was located in this pass.
Romanization note: “Guo Yingyan” is a working Mandarin pinyin romanization of 郭應言; future community correction is welcome if a church/family-preferred romanization is documented.

people/tahs-member-onboarding.title: TAHS member onboarding
people/tahs-member-onboarding.content:
TAHS Member Onboarding
TAHS Member Onboarding is the lightweight induction pathway for people who are being introduced into the Taiwanese American Historical Society (台美人歷史協會 / TAHS) and the Echopedia historical-record workflow.
This page exists to give public wiki links a stable destination. It does not publish private rosters, internal spreadsheets, personal contact details, or administrative credentials.
Public-Facing Purpose
TAHS onboarding should help a new member understand:

the mission of preserving Taiwanese American historical memory;
the role of Echopedia as a living community archive;
how identity, names, titles, and contribution records are documented carefully;
privacy expectations for personal information, family records, photos, and testimony;
how to contribute corrections, memories, documents, and source leads.

Basic Onboarding Flow

Introduction — a current TAHS/Echopedia contact introduces the person and their historical or volunteer context.
Identity confirmation — names are recorded with Chinese characters, romanized forms, and role context where available.
Consent boundary — the person should understand what can be public, what should remain private, and what needs explicit permission before publication.
Role or title note — if a formal TAHS role is assigned, record the title and scope in the appropriate society or person page only after confirmation.
Contribution path — direct the person to the community contribution hub for memories, photos, documents, corrections, and source leads.
Review loop — published records remain correctable; community members may submit updates as new evidence appears.

Privacy and Safety Rules

Do not publish private phone numbers, private email addresses, home addresses, private spreadsheets, or internal administration links.
Treat family history, immigration stories, political history, church records, and elder testimony with consent-aware care.
Prefer public source links, official documents, and contributor-approved material.
If a person asks for a correction or removal of sensitive information, route it through the Echopedia correction process.
